chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Husayn ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Al-Nawfali, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no wudu (ablution) from a mutawwa' (the place you walk on).'
Al-Nawfali said, 'It means the place on which you step with your foot.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir Al-Mu'minin (Commander of the Faithful, referring to Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the spot where you stand during wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, clarifies a technical detail in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of *wudu*: the specific spot where the foot touches the ground during the standing phase is excluded from the area of valid wiping (*masah*). This ruling ensures that the purity act is not compromised by the impurity or lack of contact precision at the point of weight-bearing, reflecting the meticulous attention to ritual mechanics in Imami fiqh.
